nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Subtropical sun drives forest and reef algae growth year round on these small islands.

nodes.name: Rain and typhoons
nodes.desc: Rain waters the islands, which have no big rivers, and typhoon winds shape the wind-clipped scrub on ridges and cliffs.

nodes.name: Warm subtropical sea
nodes.desc: Warm, clear open ocean around the islands supports reef algae, plankton and the fish that seabirds and whales feed on.

nodes.name: Island soil nutrients
nodes.desc: Thin volcanic soils are enriched by decaying leaves and by nutrients the seabirds bring in from the sea.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead leaves, carcasses and seabird remains, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Bonin screw pine
nodes.desc: An endemic screw pine of the island forests and scrub. Its fruit is eaten by the Bonin flying fox.

nodes.name: Japanese blueberry tree
nodes.desc: A common forest tree whose fruits are eaten by island birds such as the Japanese white-eye.

nodes.name: Green seaweed
nodes.desc: Sea lettuce and other algae grow on the shallow reefs and are a food for green turtles.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting microscopic algae in the open sea, the base of the food chain that reaches krill, fish and whales.

nodes.name: Bonin flying fox
nodes.desc: Endemic fruit bat of the Ogasawara and Volcano Islands, listed as endangered. It eats fruit such as Pandanus and flowers.

nodes.name: Japanese white-eye
nodes.desc: A small bird, common on the islands, that eats fruit and insects. It may compete with the flying fox for food.

nodes.name: Indian house cricket
nodes.desc: A widespread cricket that is recorded on the islands and is eaten by green anoles.

nodes.name: Black rat
nodes.desc: Introduced rodent that eats fruit, seabird eggs and chicks, and is counted among the main threats to native island wildlife.

nodes.name: Green sea turtle
nodes.desc: Adults graze seagrass and algae in shallow water. Tiger sharks are their main predator.

nodes.name: Krill
nodes.desc: Small shrimp-like plankton eaten by whales and many fish.

nodes.name: Flyingfish
nodes.desc: Surface-dwelling fish eaten by seabirds such as boobies and by larger fish.

nodes.name: Green anole
nodes.desc: Introduced American lizard. It eats small insects and was declared an invasive species in Ogasawara in 2005.

nodes.name: Eastern buzzard
nodes.desc: Bird of prey, the top flying predator on the islands, taking lizards, rodents and seabirds.

nodes.name: Bonin petrel
nodes.desc: A seabird that nests in burrows on the islands and feeds at sea. Rats and cats are predators of burrow nests.

nodes.name: Brown booby
nodes.desc: Plunge-diving seabird that feeds on flying fish and other fish near the surface.

nodes.name: Humpback whale
nodes.desc: Winters in the warm waters around the islands. It feeds mostly on krill and small fish.

nodes.name: Feral cat
nodes.desc: Introduced predator on Chichijima that kills Bonin flying foxes and seabirds.

nodes.name: Tiger shark
nodes.desc: Large shark that eats sea turtles and sometimes whale calves.
